title: dry-run plan JSON
description: Structured stdout payload emitted instead of executing a destructive operation when `--dry-run` is passed (C2). Emitted as JSON even in text mode: the point of a preview is that a machine can diff it against what it intended, and prose cannot be diffed. `--dry-run` is accepted only by `vps remove`, `vps import`, `vps edit`, `vps rename`, `sftp rm`, `sftp rmdir`, `secrets init` and `secrets reencrypt`; on any other command it is rejected with exit 64 rather than accepted and ignored.

ok.description: True: producing a plan is itself a success. A plan for an operation that would fail is not produced — preconditions that the real run checks (host exists, import validates) run first, so a refusal surfaces as the same error the real run would give.

executed.description: Always false. Present as an explicit field so a consumer never has to infer non-execution from the absence of a success event.

name.description: `vps-remove`: the host that would be removed. `vps-edit` / `vps-rename`: the name the host would have after the real run.

previous_name.description: `vps-edit` / `vps-rename`: the name the host had before this invocation. Equal to `name` when no rename was requested.

config_path.description: Registry file that would be rewritten. Absent from the `sftp-rm` and `sftp-rmdir` plans, which touch no local file.

target_resolved.description: `vps-remove` / `vps-edit` / `vps-rename`: the host the plan is about. Published only after the registry lookup succeeded, so a failed lookup carries no target. It is the name the lookup used, so for a rename plan it equals `previous_name`, not the new `name`.

target_source.description: `vps-remove` / `vps-edit` / `vps-rename`: always `argv`, because these verbs take the subject on their own command line.

source.description: `vps-import`: the file that would be read

imported.description: `vps-import`: how many hosts would be written

updated.description: `vps-edit` / `vps-rename`: the fields the real run would change, in the order they are applied. Empty when the real run would only rename the host or when every requested value already matches. `--dry-run` on an invocation with no field, rename or clear flag is refused with exit 64 before this plan is built.

active_rewritten.description: `vps-edit` / `vps-rename`: true when the sibling `active` marker points at the old name and would be rewritten, which needs a rename, false when it points elsewhere or is absent.

hosts.description: `vps-import`: one entry per host that would be written. `secrets-reencrypt`: a count of the hosts it would rewrite instead, since no host is named.

replaces_existing.description: True when a host of the same name already exists and would be overwritten. This is the field that decides whether the import is safe to run; a bare count would hide it.

incomplete.description: True when the host lacks full auth and is only accepted because of --allow-incomplete

vps.description: `sftp-rm` / `sftp-rmdir`: the registered host the operation targets

remote.description: `sftp-rm` / `sftp-rmdir`: the remote path that would be removed. Not confirmed to exist: doing so would cost a full connect and authentication, which would make the preview visible in the server's auth log exactly like a real run.

force.description: `secrets-init`: whether the primary key would be rotated

keyring.description: `secrets-init`: whether the key would be stored in the OS keyring

hosts_to_reencrypt.description: `secrets-init`: how many hosts would be re-encrypted under the new key. Always present on this plan, and 0 without `--force` or when no config file exists. Rotating without re-encrypting these would permanently lose their at-rest secrets, so the count is the number that matters before proceeding.

agent_shape.description: Present only when a global shaping flag (--select, --filter, --limit, --sort, --dedupe-by, --count-only, --truncate-content or --max-output-bytes) reduced this plan. Only the `vps-import` plan carries a collection to reduce, its `hosts` array. A reduced plan can hide the host that `replaces_existing` flags, so read that field from an unshaped plan.

input_count.description: items in the array before shaping

content_truncated.description: true when --truncate-content shortened at least one string

output_truncated.description: true when --max-output-bytes dropped items to fit the byte budget

count.description: Present only with --count-only, which replaces the `hosts` array of a `vps-import` plan by the number of items left after the other shaping flags
